reason: Re-opened packet.js veda 43 --verse 4.26.1 and the 4.26 introduction (revision 209120, pinned for 4.26). Evidence re-found verbatim: idam ādimantratrayeṇa garbhe vasan vāmadevaḥ utpannatattvajñānaḥ san sārvātmyaṃ svānubhavaṃ manvādirūpeṇa pradarśayann āha; paramārthadṛṣṭyā kṛtsnam apy aham evāsmi; he janāḥ mā māṃ sarvātmakaṃ paśyata; yūyam apy evam eva svasvarūpam anubhavata. Each clause of the reading is carried (in the womb, knowing the truth, self of all, bidding the people experience their own nature so; know for anubhavata is a fair English). The introduction and the gloss (ahaṃ vāmadeva indro vā) also allow Indra as speaker; the entry states the reading Sāyaṇa develops on the verse and claims no exclusivity, so it is not false; with first removed the earlier ambiguity is gone. Plain sense: day.js shows 4.26.1 to 3 in the first person and 4.26.4 to 7 praising the Falcon who brought the Soma. verse.js ok (4.26.1, at [321,1], 28 words); entry-check ok. No school, comparison or tone issue; Wilson’s pantheistic remark is not used.
better: If the cap allows, name the alternative Sāyaṇa keeps: “...hears in them Vāmadeva (or Indra), still in the womb...”; the womb clause belongs to the Vāmadeva reading only, so the parenthesis must not attach it to Indra.
